correctness.rationale: For the attracting harmonic responses, the dry sets are arcs of half-widths arccos(c alpha) and arccos(c beta) separated by d. Their overlap is min(2h1,h1+h2−d) up to the slow-class cutoff; for x>0 the branches meet at c=1/(alpha beta), where h1=arctan(x/rho), h2=arctan(x). On the partial-overlap branch, 2π J_x=B−S, with B>0 exactly for x>sqrt(rho), strict increase of S in c and B−S<0 at the branch junction. The resulting analytic root tends to zero at both ends of the frequency interval, so its positive maximum is interior and strictly below sqrt(rho)/(rho+1). At equality the derivative cannot vanish on an interval (analytic nonconstant root), and the nested branch decreases strictly. Below the maximum a positive derivative interval lies between the initial and terminal decreases. For epsilon=rho−1, c_rho/epsilon is bounded above by (x²−rho)/(x sqrt(1+x²)(rho²+x²)), which controls both x→1 and x→∞ uniformly. On the remaining compact frequencies S/c tends uniformly to 2x/sqrt(1+x²) and B/epsilon to (x²−1)/(1+x²)², giving uniform convergence to the stated profile and convergence of every maximizing frequency by its unique interior maximum. The witness has B=1/20 and S<1/33 at (rho,x,c)=(2,2,1/50), strictly on the partial branch. A bounded independent root bisection and local peak search gave about 0.04338458 at rho=2; that computation is only diagnostic. The x=0 value is the right-hand limit of the periodic phase statistic, not a physical static-forcing cycle. value.rationale: Each class's exposure shrinks, yet their joint exposure can recover as the relative lag shrinks after its maximum at x=sqrt(rho). The exact boundary distinguishes when this counterintuitive behavior is possible for every rate ratio and locates its scale for nearly equal rates, rather than just displaying one numerical curve. This is a useful diagnostic for coupled threshold observations in the specified harmonic model, not empirical fuel validation or an ignition/spread prediction.
